name: Ileostomy Reversal
overview: Restoration of bowel continuity after temporary ileostomy

pimpingQuestions.question: What preoperative study is mandatory before ileostomy reversal?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Water-soluble contrast enema (Gastrografin) to confirm anastomotic integrity, absence of stricture, and distal segment patency. Also endoscopy if cancer was the original indication. Never reverse if there is a leak or significant stricture.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the technique for local ileostomy reversal?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Circumferential skin incision, mobilization from the fascial defect, resection of the stoma segment (fresh bowel edges), and either hand-sewn or stapled side-to-side functional end-to-end reanastomosis through the stoma wound. The fascial defect is closed primarily.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the blood supply to the reanastomosed ileum?
pimpingQuestions.answer: SMA via ileal branches. The stoma segment is resected back to healthy, well-perfused bowel with brisk bleeding at the cut edges. The mesentery must be intact without twist.

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the most common complication after ileostomy reversal?
pimpingQuestions.answer: Small bowel obstruction (5-10%) -- the most common cause of readmission. Adhesions at the stoma site and internal herniation through the mesenteric defect are the usual mechanisms. Wound infection (5-15%), anastomotic leak (1-3%), and prolonged ileus (5-10%).

pimpingQuestions.question: What is the optimal timing for ileostomy reversal?
pimpingQuestions.answer: 8-12 weeks after the index operation (allows inflammation to resolve and anastomosis to mature). After neoadjuvant chemoradiation for rectal cancer, many surgeons wait 12-16 weeks. Confirm completion of adjuvant chemotherapy before reversal when applicable.
